subject.title: [Bug]: sandbox-browser noVNC clipboard garbles non-Latin-1 characters (CJK, Cyrillic, etc.)

question: Should OpenClaw replace the sandbox-browser VNC server stack for UTF-8 Extended Clipboard, or solve non-Latin input through a different security-preserving path?
rationale: The bug is source-supported, but the likely fix changes the VNC/display-server boundary and must preserve password auth, loopback exposure, token bootstrap, and image-contract behavior.

options.title: Sponsor secured TigerVNC replacement
options.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with a VNC server that supports Extended Clipboard while preserving auth, localhost binding, noVNC token flow, startup lifecycle, and live paste proof.

options.title: Solve via browser text insertion
options.body: Keep the current noVNC stack and route non-Latin input through a browser/CDP insertion action, accepting that the noVNC clipboard panel remains limited.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Leave x11vnc in place and document the noVNC UTF-8 clipboard limitation until a sandbox-browser owner chooses a repair direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor secured TigerVNC replacement
recommendation.body: Replace x11vnc/Xvfb with a VNC server that supports Extended Clipboard while preserving auth, localhost binding, noVNC token flow, startup lifecycle, and live paste proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the sandbox-browser feature and the noVNC auth/token hardening that any VNC-stack replacement must preserve.
